comparisons.evidence: P spans late-bound access, checkpointed care, transferable rights, third-party permission and demand relocation—e.g. “Leave Clearance First,” “Neighborhood Pop-Up Batch” and “Reverse Appointment.” Q is diverse, but several survivors remain variants of pre-visit communication, fallback routing or schedule flexibility.

P reaches mechanisms such as “appointment entitlement transferable within an eligible household,” “exact slot assigned only after the patient begins travelling” and care beginning “before deciding whether an appointment is needed.” Q retains more readily generated ideas such as a “readiness handshake,” “micro-commitment” and virtual queuing.

P names rules—“graceful degradation,” “checkpointing,” “late binding” and kidney-exchange “chains”—then states which ideas “depend on” each rule and rejects decorative borrowing such as “Appointment blockchain.” Q names useful rules, but provides less analysis of indispensability or failed analogies.

P’s choice directly reduces timing fragility by replacing “exact-time compliance with late-bound service access.” Q’s choice identifies the “recoverable state” of an “unsure” patient and couples it with protected release and refilling. Both are credible practical leaders, with different operational risks.

P gives every survivor a specific “Assumption that must hold” and a measurable “Cheapest falsification,” including explicit kill conditions such as demand being “too dispersed to fill a half-day mobile session.” Q lists genuine failure modes, but mostly stops at labels such as “low response rates” or “operational complexity.”

P states compact causal reversals: “Scarcity can increase no-shows,” “precision transfers all timing risk to the patient,” and “A no-show is partly a property of service design.” Q also has strong insights—especially “an ‘unsure’ patient is not yet a no-show”—but they are less consistently sharp across its recommendations.

note: P’s biggest advantage is mechanism-level originality backed by explicit falsification; Q’s strongest advantage is a coherent, implementation-ready combined pilot.
